events.title: First arrival at Madjedbebe
events.description: Stone tools and ground ochre under a rock shelter in Arnhem Land give the oldest secure date for people in Australia, and one of the oldest for modern humans outside Africa.

events.title: The megafauna disappear
events.description: Diprotodon, a marsupial lion and a three-metre kangaroo vanish within a few thousand years of human arrival. How much was hunting and how much was climate is still argued.

events.title: The burials at Lake Mungo
events.description: A cremation and an ochred burial beside a lake that is now dry are among the earliest ritual human burials known anywhere.

events.title: The rock art of Murujuga
events.description: The Burrup peninsula holds perhaps a million petroglyphs, including images of animals that have been extinct for thousands of years.

events.title: The glacial maximum
events.description: Sea level is a hundred and twenty metres lower, Tasmania and New Guinea are joined to the mainland, and the interior is colder and far drier than now.

events.title: Tasmania is cut off
events.description: Rising seas flood the Bassian plain. The people of Tasmania are isolated for four hundred generations, the longest isolation of any human population.

events.title: The eel traps at Budj Bim
events.description: Gunditjmara people cut channels and weirs through lava flow to farm eels, and build stone houses beside them. It is aquaculture older than the pyramids.

events.title: The dingo arrives
events.description: Australia's only placental land predator before Europeans comes by sea with Asian seafarers, and reshapes the ecology of the mainland.

events.title: Songlines and the Dreaming
events.description: Law, geography and genealogy are carried in song cycles that run for hundreds of kilometres across the country and hand between language groups at the boundary.

events.title: Makassan trade with Arnhem Land
events.description: Praus from Sulawesi come south each monsoon for trepang, trading iron, cloth and tobacco. It is regular international commerce, and it predates the British by centuries.

events.title: The Duyfken makes landfall
events.description: Willem Janszoon charts part of Cape York for the Dutch, takes it for a southern extension of New Guinea, and loses men in the first recorded clash with Aboriginal people.

events.title: Torres sails the strait
events.description: Luis Vaez de Torres passes between New Guinea and Cape York without apparently realising a continent lies to the south. The strait carries his name.

events.title: Dirk Hartog leaves a plate
events.description: A Dutch captain nails an inscribed pewter dish to a post on a Western Australian island. It is the oldest known European artefact in Australia.

events.title: The wreck of the Batavia
events.description: A Dutch East India ship strikes a reef and the survivors are subjected to a mutiny and a massacre. Two men are marooned on the mainland and never seen again.

events.title: Tasman charts Van Diemen's Land
events.description: Abel Tasman finds Tasmania and New Zealand while sailing around the continent without seeing its east coast, and concludes it is not worth much.

events.title: Dampier on the northwest coast
events.description: An English buccaneer spends weeks on the Kimberley shore and writes it up so unfavourably that it discourages British interest for eighty years.

events.title: Cook charts the east coast
events.description: The Endeavour maps two thousand miles of coastline, nearly sinks on the Great Barrier Reef, and its naturalists collect a flora nobody in Europe has seen.

events.title: Possession Island
events.description: Cook claims the whole eastern coast for Britain from an island off Cape York, on the legal fiction that the land belongs to nobody.

events.title: Botany Bay chosen for a penal colony
events.description: With American independence closing the old destination for transported convicts, the British cabinet picks a harbour on the other side of the world on a decade-old report.

events.title: The First Fleet arrives
events.description: Eleven ships and about fourteen hundred people, more than half of them convicts, land at Sydney Cove after Botany Bay proves unsuitable. Australia Day and Invasion Day are the same date.

events.title: Smallpox devastates the Eora
events.description: An epidemic kills perhaps half the Aboriginal people around Sydney within a year. Its origin has never been settled and the argument is not academic.

events.title: The Second Fleet
events.description: Contractors paid per head embarked rather than landed deliver a quarter of their convicts dead and most of the rest unable to walk. The scandal forces reform of the trade.

events.title: Pemulwuy's resistance
events.description: A Bidjigal man leads twelve years of raids against the settlements around Sydney. He is shot in 1802 and his head is sent to England.

events.title: The first free settlers
events.description: A handful of families arrive with land grants and convict labour. The colony starts becoming a society rather than a prison.

events.title: Merino sheep are landed
events.description: John Macarthur and others import Spanish merinos. Within fifty years wool is the reason the colony pays for itself.

events.title: Settlement at Risdon Cove
events.description: The British occupy Van Diemen's Land to forestall the French. Within thirty years the Aboriginal population of the island is almost entirely destroyed.

events.title: The Castle Hill rebellion
events.description: Several hundred mostly Irish convicts rise and are broken in fifteen minutes by the New South Wales Corps. Nine are hanged.

events.title: The Rum Rebellion
events.description: Officers of the New South Wales Corps depose Governor Bligh. It is the only successful armed takeover of government in Australian history.

events.title: Macquarie begins building
events.description: A new governor puts up roads, hospitals and public buildings, employs emancipated convicts, and is recalled for treating them as citizens.

events.title: The Blue Mountains are crossed
events.description: Blaxland, Lawson and Wentworth find a route along the ridges rather than the valleys. The inland grasslands open and pastoral expansion begins.

events.title: The Bank of New South Wales
events.description: The colony gets its first bank, and eventually a currency that is not measured in rum.

events.title: Moreton Bay penal settlement
events.description: A place of secondary punishment is founded at what becomes Brisbane. Free settlement is banned within eighty kilometres for another two decades.

events.title: Martial law in Van Diemen's Land
events.description: The Black War brings a declaration of martial law against Aboriginal Tasmanians, then a failed human chain across the island to drive them into a corner.

events.title: The Swan River Colony
events.description: Western Australia is settled as a free colony without convicts. It struggles so badly for labour that it asks for convicts twenty years later.

events.title: Batman's treaty and the founding of Melbourne
events.description: John Batman claims to buy six hundred thousand acres from Kulin elders for blankets and tomahawks. The governor voids it, because only the Crown may acquire land.

events.title: South Australia is proclaimed
events.description: A colony designed by Wakefield on paper: no convicts, land sold rather than granted, and religious freedom written in from the start.

events.title: The Myall Creek massacre
events.description: Twenty-eight Wirrayaraay people are killed by stockmen. Seven of the killers are hanged, the only such convictions of the century, and the frontier learns to leave no evidence.

events.title: Transportation to New South Wales ends
events.description: Eighty thousand convicts have been landed in the colony. Free immigrants now outnumber them and want the stigma gone.

events.title: Eyre crosses the Nullarbor
events.description: Edward Eyre walks two thousand kilometres along the Great Australian Bight, surviving because his Aboriginal companion Wylie keeps finding water.

events.title: Ludwig Leichhardt reaches Port Essington
events.description: A German naturalist crosses from the Darling Downs to Arnhem Land, is given a hero's welcome, and vanishes without trace on his next attempt.

events.title: The squatters get their runs
events.description: Pastoralists who had simply occupied land beyond the settled districts are granted long leases over it. The frontier is legalised after the fact.

events.title: Gold is found near Bathurst
events.description: Edward Hargraves publicises a find at Ophir and the colonies empty into the diggings. Victoria's population triples in three years.

events.title: Victoria separates from New South Wales
events.description: The Port Phillip district becomes its own colony weeks before the gold rush makes it the richest place in the empire.

events.title: The Chinese arrive on the goldfields
events.description: Tens of thousands come from Guangdong. Within five years the colonies begin passing the entry taxes and residence laws that become the White Australia policy.

events.title: The Eureka Stockade
events.description: Ballarat diggers burn their licences and build a stockade over mining fees and the vote. Twenty-two are killed, every man tried is acquitted, and the licence is abolished.

events.title: Responsible government
events.description: New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Tasmania get elected parliaments running their own affairs. It is remarkably early by any standard.

events.title: The eight hour day
events.description: Stonemasons on the Melbourne University site down tools and win eight hours work, eight hours recreation and eight hours rest. It is one of the first such wins anywhere.

events.title: Manhood suffrage in Victoria
events.description: Every adult male gets the vote and the secret ballot is already in use. The Australian ballot is exported to Britain and the United States.

events.title: Queensland separates
events.description: The northern districts become a colony. The frontier there is the most violent in Australia and the Native Police are the instrument of it.

events.title: Burke and Wills set out
events.description: A lavishly funded expedition crosses the continent and both leaders die at Cooper Creek, beside a tree carved with the word DIG, having failed to eat what the Yandruwandha ate.

events.title: The Lambing Flat riots
events.description: White miners drive Chinese diggers off the field at Young. The colonial response is to restrict Chinese immigration rather than to protect them.

events.title: The last convict ship
events.description: The Hougoumont lands at Fremantle. Eighty years and about a hundred and sixty-two thousand transported convicts come to an end.

events.title: The first Australian cricket tour of England
events.description: An all-Aboriginal team plays forty-seven matches in a season. They are not allowed to represent Australia again for over a century.

events.title: The Overland Telegraph
events.description: Three thousand kilometres of wire from Adelaide to Darwin connect Australia to London. A message that took two months now takes hours.

events.title: The first Test match
events.description: Australia beats England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground by forty-five runs. The Ashes follow five years later, after an obituary for English cricket.

events.title: Ned Kelly at Glenrowan
events.description: A bushranger in homemade plate armour is taken after a siege and hanged at eleven. Whether he is a folk hero or a murderer has been argued ever since.

events.title: Silver at Broken Hill
events.description: A boundary rider pegs a claim on a broken hill of ore. BHP is founded on it and becomes the largest company in the country.

events.title: The centenary, and the colour bar
events.description: A hundred years of settlement is celebrated while the colonies coordinate to exclude Chinese immigrants. Aboriginal people are not counted in either conversation.

events.title: The maritime strike
events.description: A shearers and seamen's dispute spreads across the colonies and is defeated. Out of the defeat the unions decide to form a political party.

events.title: The shearers' strike at Barcaldine
events.description: Troopers break a shearers' camp in central Queensland. The Australian Labor Party traces itself to a tree in that town.

events.title: Gold at Coolgardie and Kalgoorlie
events.description: A rush into the Western Australian desert with almost no water. A pipeline five hundred and sixty kilometres long is built to supply it.

events.title: South Australian women win the vote
events.description: They also win the right to stand for parliament, which no women anywhere else had. New Zealand had granted the vote a year earlier without the second half.

events.title: Waltzing Matilda
events.description: Banjo Paterson writes a song about a swagman who drowns himself rather than be taken. It becomes the country's unofficial anthem.

events.title: The federation referendums
events.description: Colonial voters approve a constitution drafted by their own elected conventions. Australia federates by argument and ballot rather than by war.

events.title: Federation
events.description: Six colonies become one Commonwealth. Aboriginal people are explicitly excluded from the census and from the new parliament's power to legislate for them.

events.title: The Immigration Restriction Act
events.description: The new parliament's first substantial law screens migrants with a dictation test in any European language. White Australia is the policy for seventy years.

events.title: Women get the federal vote
events.description: Australian women can vote and stand for the national parliament before those in any other self-governing country. Aboriginal women and men are excluded.

events.title: The Harvester judgment
events.description: A court rules a wage must keep a labourer, a wife and three children in frugal comfort. The basic wage is the foundation of Australian industrial relations for eighty years.

events.title: The old age pension
events.description: A national pension is legislated seven years after federation, ahead of most of the world.

events.title: Canberra is named
events.description: A capital is built from nothing on a site chosen because Sydney and Melbourne would not accept each other. Walter and Marion Griffin win the design competition.

events.title: Australia enters the Great War
events.description: A population of fewer than five million sends over four hundred thousand volunteers. Sixty thousand do not come back.

events.title: The Gallipoli landing
events.description: A failed campaign on a Turkish peninsula becomes the national story, commemorated every year on the date of the landing rather than any victory.

events.title: The conscription referendums
events.description: Two plebiscites on compulsory overseas service are both narrowly defeated, splitting the Labor Party and the country along sectarian lines.

events.title: Beersheba
events.description: The Australian Light Horse charges Turkish trenches and takes the wells. It is one of the last effective cavalry charges in history.

events.title: Villers-Bretonneux
events.description: Australian troops retake the town on the third anniversary of the landing. Monash's combined-arms methods at Hamel three months later are studied for decades.

events.title: The influenza pandemic
events.description: Quarantine keeps it out for months and about fifteen thousand die when it lands. Returning troops bring it home with them.

events.title: Qantas is founded
events.description: An air service starts at Winton to connect western Queensland stations. It becomes the oldest continuously operating airline outside the Netherlands.

events.title: The Country Party enters coalition
events.description: Rural interests get a permanent seat at the table. The arrangement between the conservative parties still runs a century later.

events.title: Parliament moves to Canberra
events.description: The federal parliament finally leaves Melbourne for the provisional building in its own capital.

events.title: The Coniston massacre
events.description: At least thirty-one Warlpiri, Anmatyerre and Kaytetye people are killed by a police party in the Northern Territory. It is the last known frontier massacre and the officer is exonerated.

events.title: The Flying Doctor
events.description: John Flynn's aerial medical service starts at Cloncurry, using pedal radios to reach stations a week's ride from anywhere.

events.title: Phar Lap wins the Melbourne Cup
events.description: A horse becomes a Depression-era folk hero, then dies in California in circumstances people still argue about.

events.title: The Depression bites
events.description: Unemployment reaches nearly a third. The Premiers' Plan cuts wages and spending, and the Labor Party splits over it.

events.title: The Sydney Harbour Bridge opens
events.description: A right-wing paramilitary slashes the ribbon on horseback before the premier can cut it. The bridge itself was built through the worst of the Depression.

events.title: The Emu War
events.description: Soldiers with machine guns are sent against emus in Western Australia and lose. It is genuinely funny and it was a genuine agricultural crisis.

events.title: The Day of Mourning
events.description: Aboriginal activists hold a protest in Sydney on the sesquicentenary and demand citizenship and equality. It is the beginning of organised national Aboriginal politics.

events.title: Australia is at war again
events.description: Menzies announces that because Britain has declared war, Australia is also at war. The phrasing dates the relationship precisely.

events.title: Curtin turns to America
events.description: With Japan in the war the prime minister says Australia looks to the United States free of any pangs about its traditional links with Britain.

events.title: Singapore falls
events.description: Fifteen thousand Australians go into Japanese captivity. A third of the prisoners taken do not survive the war.

events.title: Darwin is bombed
events.description: Two raids by more aircraft than were used at Pearl Harbor kill at least two hundred and forty-three people. The scale is censored at the time.

events.title: The Coral Sea and the Kokoda Track
events.description: A carrier battle turns back the seaborne threat to Port Moresby, and militia and regulars fight the Japanese to a standstill along a mountain track.

events.title: The war ends
events.description: Nearly a million Australians served and about thirty-nine thousand died. The country comes out of it aligned with Washington rather than London.

events.title: Populate or perish
events.description: A mass immigration programme opens to displaced Europeans, then to southern Europe. Two million arrive in twenty years and the country stops being British.

events.title: The first Holden
events.description: A car designed for Australian roads is built at Fishermans Bend. It is the industrial confidence of the postwar decades in one object.

events.title: The Snowy Mountains Scheme
events.description: Sixteen dams, a hundred and forty-five kilometres of tunnels and twenty-five years of work, built largely by migrant labour from thirty countries.

events.title: The ANZUS treaty
events.description: Australia, New Zealand and the United States sign a security pact. It replaces the assumption that Britain would be there.

events.title: The referendum to ban the Communist Party
events.description: Menzies asks for the power to outlaw a political party and is narrowly refused. Australians decline to hand over that particular tool.

events.title: The Melbourne Olympics and television
events.description: The games come to the southern hemisphere for the first time, and television is switched on a few weeks before them.

events.title: British nuclear tests at Maralinga
events.description: Britain detonates weapons on Anangu land with Australian consent. The traditional owners are inadequately warned and the site is not properly cleaned for forty years.

events.title: Aboriginal people get the federal vote
events.description: The Commonwealth Electoral Act is amended. Voting is optional for them and compulsory for everyone else, which tells you the state of the argument.

events.title: The Freedom Ride
events.description: Charles Perkins and Sydney students bus through country New South Wales and force segregation at pools and cinemas into the newspapers.

events.title: The Wave Hill walk-off
events.description: Gurindji stockmen strike over wages and stay out for nine years, turning the dispute into a land claim. It becomes the start of the land rights movement.

events.title: The 1967 referendum
events.description: More than ninety per cent vote to count Aboriginal people in the census and let the Commonwealth legislate for them. It is the largest yes vote in Australian history.

events.title: The Aboriginal Tent Embassy
events.description: Four men put a beach umbrella on the lawn opposite Parliament House to protest that they are treated as aliens in their own country. It is still there.

events.title: Whitlam is elected
events.description: Twenty-three years of conservative government end. Conscription is abolished, university fees are dropped and universal health insurance is legislated within three years.

events.title: The Sydney Opera House opens
events.description: Fourteen years late, fifteen times over budget, and the architect is not invited. It is on the world heritage list within a generation.

events.title: The White Australia policy formally ends
events.description: The last racial criteria are removed from immigration law. Within two years Vietnamese refugees are arriving by boat.

events.title: Cyclone Tracy destroys Darwin
events.description: Seventy-one people die and most of the city is flattened on Christmas Eve. Thirty thousand are evacuated in the largest airlift in Australian history.

events.title: The Dismissal
events.description: The governor-general sacks an elected prime minister over a blocked budget. It is the deepest constitutional crisis the country has had and it is resolved by an election.

events.title: Land rights in the Northern Territory
events.description: The Fraser government legislates the first Aboriginal land rights act, granting inalienable freehold title over reserves.

events.title: The dollar is floated
events.description: The Hawke government floats the currency, then deregulates banking and cuts tariffs, with union agreement bought through the Accord.

events.title: The Franklin Dam is stopped
events.description: The High Court blocks a Tasmanian dam using the external affairs power and a world heritage listing. Environmental politics arrives as a national force.

events.title: Medicare
events.description: Universal health insurance is restored after being dismantled, and this time it survives every change of government since.

events.title: The Mabo decision
events.description: The High Court finds that native title survived British settlement, overturning terra nullius after two hundred and four years. Eddie Mabo had died five months earlier.

events.title: Port Arthur and the gun laws
events.description: Thirty-five people are killed by one man. Within twelve days every state agrees to a firearms ban and buyback, and there is no comparable massacre for over twenty years.

events.title: The Bringing Them Home report
events.description: An inquiry documents the removal of Aboriginal children from their families over decades. The government of the day refuses to apologise.

events.title: The republic referendum
events.description: Australians vote to keep the monarchy, with many republicans voting no because they wanted a directly elected president rather than one chosen by parliament.

events.title: The Sydney Olympics
events.description: Cathy Freeman lights the cauldron and wins the four hundred metres. A quarter of a million people had walked across the bridge for reconciliation four months earlier.

events.title: The Apology
events.description: Kevin Rudd apologises in parliament to the Stolen Generations. It is broadcast to crowds in every capital and costs nothing anybody had claimed it would.

events.title: Black Saturday
events.description: Bushfires in Victoria kill one hundred and seventy-three people in a day, the deadliest in Australian history.

events.title: Same-sex marriage
events.description: A voluntary postal survey returns sixty-two per cent yes on an eighty per cent turnout, and parliament legislates within three weeks.

events.title: The Black Summer
events.description: Fires burn twenty-four million hectares over months, kill or displace an estimated three billion animals, and put smoke over the east coast for weeks.

events.title: The Voice referendum
events.description: A proposal for an Indigenous advisory body in the constitution is defeated in every state, with about sixty per cent voting no.
